title: Male borrowers using the phrase 'has asked for a loan' fund faster than those saying 'wants to take out a loan'.
Male borrowers who mention specific institutional names in their pitches may fund more slowly.
Mentioning existing asset ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who express direct gratitude to lenders may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention the loan amount in local currency may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who explicitly state their age in the pitch may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who detail specific community volunteering commitments may fund more slowly.
Pitches from women that specify the loan amount using local currency denominations, such as PHP, are associated with slower funding speeds.
Female borrowers who mention specific educational goals or school status for children may fund more slowly.
Male borrowers who emphasize family partnership and specify child ages may fund faster.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention a history of successful loans from NWTF fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Female borrowers who link loan purposes to both education and business income fund faster.
